Area.evidence_source: When it comes to the healthcare services, most participants experienced lack of knowledge and understanding regarding consequences of sexual violence against men and boys, especially within the mental healthcare services. This is consistent with Easton's study (33) that many healthcare professionals are unequipped to provide appropriate assistance to male victims because of their lack of knowledge and understanding. Since all participants struggled with health problems, healthcare professionals need to become more knowledgeable about consequences of sexual violence. To improve mental health services for male victims, the seriousness of the sexual violence must be kept in mind and professionals must be aware of masculine norms and their negative impact on male emotional life, which can even be life-threatening (8).; Psychological treatment, pharmacological treatment and neurological treatment of psychiatric problems can prevent suicidality, and therefore, it is also important that mental health professionals provide quality follow-up after treatment of clients who have attempted suicide (2). Interestingly, the participants mentioned that healthcare professionals need to be more adept in asking clients about their traumas. If healthcare professionals do not ask men about trauma following sexual violence, it is likely that they will not get the right service, because male sexual violence survivors rarely disclose their trauma story without being asked (31).; Von Hohendorff et al. (38) interviewed psychologists who had experience in working with male sexual violence survivors. The psychologists emphasised the important protective measures against sexual violence against males and claimed that the healthcare system is defective and unprepared to address cases where boys or men are victims of sexual violence. They claim that healthcare professionals are under too much stress and strain and that the system is not able to intervene and do the necessary follow-up on such cases.
